# Activation Plan Functions

Defines the functions that validate and plan a document’s activation controls, with inherited functions for party approval, roster changes, access checks and activation state. `plan` returns contract contributions and initial state declarations; producing this plan does not itself establish installation, acceptance or activation.

## Configuration and planning

`configuration` reads `/clauseRuntime/work/candidate/<clauseKey>/parameters`, using the `clauseKey` constant. Inherited runtime functions read `/clauses/activation/parameters`. All paths refer to the document where these functions execute.

- `parties` must be a nonempty object keyed by party role. Each party needs `lead/channel`. Party roles and `representatives` keys must be nonempty text containing none of `.`, `/`, `~` or `__`. Lead transports use the role name; additional representative transports use `<role>__<representative>`.
- `required` identifies parties whose approvals are needed; it defaults to all configured party keys. An explicitly empty list requires no party approvals, but cannot enable negotiation.
- `accessPaths` defaults to `[]` and identifies embedded Timeline Access documents. `readers` defaults to `{}` and supplies additional groups of alternative reader keys. Party `readerKeys` and each additional representative’s `readerKeys` replace same-named reader groups.
- `allowNewParties` defaults to `false`. `frozen` defaults to `false`, but initial roster state is also frozen when `/partyRosterFrozen` is `true`.
- `revision` defaults to `1`; it identifies the activation revision reviewed for approval.
- `preActivationOperations` and `preActivationChannels` default to `[]`. Planning adds `approve_<role>` and `updateParty_<role>` for each configured party to the operations allowed before activation, subject to the access and closure guards below.
- `negotiation/allowedPaths` defaults to `[]`. A nonempty list enables negotiation operation generation.

The plan declares `/activation` with computed initial state and `/partyAccess` as an empty object. Initial `approved` and `accessRequests` are empty objects. It contributes party transports and operations, embedded processing for `accessPaths` and `/partyAccess`, refresh handlers, and the `activationDispatch` policy. An existing channel outside clause-runtime ownership is reused only when its contract exactly matches the planned contribution; a mismatch fails with `ACTIVATION_CHANNEL_CONFLICT`.

`Clauses Initialized` triggers refresh. Each configured access path receives an `activationAccess<index>` channel listening for `Timeline Access Updated`, followed by refresh. `Party Addition Requested` invokes `requestPartyAddition` and then refresh. Dynamically installed access documents also receive registered refresh channels.

## Access and dispatch

Access validation examines every lead and additional representative transport. An `External Channel` needs no Timeline Access match in this check. Other transports must be `Timeline Channel` values. Each such transport needs a matching Timeline Access document at an `accessPaths` location: its timeline and provider must match, and that same access document must authorize at least one key from every reader group. An empty reader group cannot satisfy this requirement. Invalid channel or access-document types fail validation.

`activationDispatch` evaluates runtime-owned `dispatch/kind`, `dispatch/channel` and `dispatch/operation` in this order:

1. Allow `TRIGGERED` delivery on `activationInitialized`, and `EMBEDDED` delivery on configured access-control channels or `/activation/registeredAccessChannels`. These exceptions permit refresh even before readiness or after closure.
2. Reject other delivery if `/activation` is absent (`ACTIVATION_NOT_INITIALIZED`), `accessReady` is not exactly `true`, or a fresh access check fails (`DOCUMENT_ACCESS_UNAVAILABLE`).
3. Reject a closed document (`DOCUMENT_CLOSED`).
4. Allow listed external `preOperations` and listed non-external `preChannels`.
5. Otherwise require `businessReady`: all required approvals, current recorded terms, valid access and an open document. Failure is reported as `DOCUMENT_NOT_ACTIVE`.

This policy’s allowance is not permission from every installed policy or operation. A denied delivery skips its handlers; external input is still consumed and checkpointed, not queued for replay after activation.

## Approval and party changes

`approve_<role>` operates on the party’s lead channel. Approval requires `call/requireExactDocumentVersion` to be `true`, an input `revision` matching `/activation/revision`, and valid participant access. With negotiation enabled, `termsRef` must be text identifying `/activation/terms/ref`; any supplied mismatching reference is rejected. Repeating an already-recorded approval returns successfully without another acceptance event.

A new approval records `approved[role]`, commits recomputed state and emits `Terms Accepted` with `party` and `revision`. One party’s acceptance does not establish activation. If the commit yields an active document, an outstanding negotiation proposal is marked `SUPERSEDED` and cleared, and `negotiation/editable` becomes `false`.

`updateParty_<role>` accepts `replacement`, including `lead/channel`, and optional `party`. Omission targets the invoking party; adding a party requires its explicit new key. No input revision is required, but exact document review is. Only an existing party lead may manage its own existing party; adding another party requires `allowNewParties`. Frozen rosters, invalid names, missing lead channels, insufficient access for the replacement roster and conflicting contract names are rejected.

A successful update installs the new roster contracts, clears all approvals, increments `revision`, and appends a newly added party to `required`. It commits state and emits `Party Changed`. Listing a representative or exposing an operation does not grant that representative every party operation.

Approved admission is a separate inherited route. `admitApprovedParties` requires an unfrozen roster, matching `expectedRevision`, nonempty configured `admission/approvers`, compatible main identities and valid access for the resulting roster. Main identity matching requires the same lead channel and the same nonempty, duplicate-free set of primary `readerKeys`. The function checks that an admission policy exists; it does not itself collect its approvals. An unchanged roster returns `duplicate`; a new admission installs contracts, increments the revision and emits `Party Changed` with `kind: Participants admitted` and `admissionRef`. This route does not automatically append admitted roles to `required`.

`requestPartyAddition` ignores stale revisions and already-recorded `admissionRef` values. It validates supplied `accessDocuments`, embeds new public access histories under `/partyAccess`, and records pending additions under `/activation/accessRequests`. Missing access for existing parties produces `Party Access Update Requested` events. These are requests, not grants, admission completion or participant consent. Permission changes remain provider-owned. Access installation accepts 1–16 documents per call, verifies initialization, provider history and the expected executable contracts, and deduplicates histories by their origin.

## Negotiated terms

Allowed negotiation paths must be unique absolute paths with nonempty segments and no `~`. Their first segment cannot be `clauses`, `contracts`, `activation`, `clauseRuntime`, `type`, `name` or `description`. A path cannot equal or descend from a configured access path. Initialization requires each selected field to exist and contain text, integer, double or Boolean data.

Enabling negotiation additionally requires nonempty negotiators (`required`, defaulting to all parties), a document `/type`, and candidate `negotiationDefinition/functions` containing `proposeChanges`. Planning adds a `validTermsCandidate` matcher against the document type and generates, for each negotiator, `proposeChanges_<role>`, `proposeAndActivate_<role>`, `activate_<role>`, `withdrawProposal_<role>`, `rejectProposal_<role>` and `withdrawAcceptance_<role>`. These invoke the corresponding `Public` functions with `call/request`, binding `state` to `/activation/negotiation`, `editable` to `/activation/negotiation/editable`, and the amendment target to `/activation/terms/fields`.

Proposal requests carry `baseTermsRef`, a unique `proposalId`, and a nonempty `changes` list. Each change has required `path` and `replacement`; the path identifies an allowed term, and replacement typing follows the current term definition. `supersedes` identifies the current proposal when replacing one. Selection requests carry `termsRef`, with `proposalId` omitted for current terms and included for proposed terms. Withdrawal and rejection identify the selected proposal.

Terms initialization records allowed field values in `/activation/terms/fields` and a reference in `/activation/terms/ref`. Its fixed definition identity derives from the initial document after removing negotiated fields, access documents, activation `accessPaths` and `readers`, and party-level `readerKeys`. It initializes `termsRevision` and negotiation `revision` to `1`, `editable` to `true`, and `history`, `outcomes` and `proposal` to empty objects. Existing terms are preserved.

When parties or required approvers change after terms exist, committing state updates the terms identity, increments `termsRevision`, clears an outstanding proposal with outcome `AUTHORITY_CHANGED`, and clears approvals when negotiation is enabled.

`validateTransition` rejects any candidate clause-set change while existing activation configuration enables negotiation and `everActivated` is not `true` (`NEGOTIATION_POLICY_LOCKED`). Otherwise, this activation clause must remain unchanged; changes are rejected with `USE_ACTIVATION_PARTY_OPERATIONS`.

## State and outcomes

`computeState` derives `/activation/accessReady` and `functional` from access validation, including pending additions whose `expectedRevision` still matches. `termsAccepted` means every `required` role has recorded approval and each stored terms field still equals its corresponding document value. `active` additionally requires valid access and an open document.

`status` is `CLOSED`, `WAITING_FOR_ACCESS`, `SUSPENDED_ACCESS`, `AWAITING_ACCEPTANCE` or `ACTIVE`. `everActivated` records whether activation has ever occurred, so it does not establish present readiness. `reason` reports `PARTICIPANT_ACCESS_MISSING`, `ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED` or an empty string; it does not independently describe closure. Missing approvals are treated as unapproved by these checks. Configuration defaults describe initialization, not evidence that absent runtime state exists.

Committing state emits `Document Activated` on first activation, `Document Access Suspended` when an active document loses access, and `Document Access Restored` when it becomes active after previously having unavailable access. These events carry the activation revision. Refresh also updates pending access-request readiness and reconciles initial party channels, using empty composite channels until access is ready.

The supplied negotiation function library bodies are not shown, so their additional rejection rules and proposal-to-activation effects are not established here. An operation request or access notification alone does not establish its committed outcome.
